title: Berapa harga ni?
blurb: Asking prices at a fruit stall, and tasting before you buy.

notes.title: Berapa?
notes.body: Berapa asks how much or how many. Berapa harga ni? — how much is this? At a stall, pointing and saying Berapa? is enough.

notes.title: sekilo, sebiji
notes.body: se- means “one”: sekilo = one kilo, sebiji = one (piece of fruit). Prices are usually per kilo: dua belas ringgit sekilo.

notes.title: Cuba rasa dulu
notes.body: “Try a taste first.” Fruit sellers will often offer; manis tak? (is it sweet?) is the question that gets you a sample.

tr.Ada lagi. Nak berapa kilo?: There's still some. How many kilos do you want?
tr.Apa kau nak beli?: What do you want to buy?
It only came in this morning.
tr.Biru je ada. Nak cuba?: There's only blue. Want to try them?
Okay then, I'll try them first.
tr.Boleh saya tinggal satu barang?: Can I leave one item behind?
tr.Cili nak berapa?: How much chilli do you want?

The green ones. They're a bit cheaper.
Eighty ringgit. It's the original product.
